subject: All 17 MEDIUM and 7 LOW new findings (N-04..N-21 excluding HIGH N-01, N-02, N-03, N-15)
independence_note: Every finding was re-evaluated against read-only V2.1 source and, where useful, independently executed read-only probes. No V2.1 test result or report was accepted as proof of closure. No finding was automatically closed; original severities are preserved verbatim.

classification_definitions.A: must fix before Stage B readiness

classification_note: No lower-severity finding maps to B or C: both recruitment_authorized and field_validation_authorized are hard-coded False in V2.1 (engine/validator.py:83-84, 565) and none of these findings can flip either flag. A is used where a semantically invalid state is still reported stage_b_role_ready=True; D where the defect is fail-closed or diagnostics-only; E where an authoritative source, policy or identity design decision is required before a gate decision can be made.

findings.title: Whitespace-only escalation contact accepted
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged from V2. engine/validator.py:475-476 still tests `if not rec.get('escalation',{}).get('contact')`, so any non-empty string, including '   ', is treated as a present escalation contact. The V2.1 meaningful_text() gate introduced for N-01/N-02 (validator.py:51-53) was NOT applied here. Schema line 119 types contact as ['string','null'] with no minLength/pattern. Read-only probe on V2.1 tests/fixtures/valid_four_person.json with RESEARCH_OWNER escalation.contact='   ' returned stage_b_role_ready=True, onboarding_readiness=PASS, zero issues.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: yes — a role with no substantive escalation contact is reported Stage B ready (independent probe: ready=True, 0 issues); this misstates the onboarding dimension and the aggregate readiness flag.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: authorization integrity yes (a readiness claim is emitted without the required contact); confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Apply meaningful_text() to escalation.contact in validator.py:475-476 (emit E-ESCALATION-CONTACT for whitespace/non-string), add minLength/pattern or a dedicated format to schema line 119, and add a regression case equivalent to harness ST-10.

findings.title: Duplicate roles inside a combination approval are accepted
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged. pair_key() at validator.py:256-257 uses '+'.join(sorted(set(roles))), so ['RESEARCH_OWNER','CONTINUE_STOP_OWNER','CONTINUE_STOP_OWNER'] collapses to the same key as the correct two-role pair. approval_map keying (503-511) and the held-set lookup (533-537) therefore match and no duplicate error is emitted. Schema line 136 declares roles as a plain string array with no uniqueItems. Probe: duplicate-role mutation of valid_four_person.json returned ready=True, 0 issues (also recorded as COMB-03 DEFECT in V2.1 tests/results/independent_adversarial_results.json).
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: yes technically (ready=True) but not materially: set semantics mean the exact two-role combination is still approved; no third role or extra person is introduced and no unsupported appointment is created.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — the effective approval is bound to the same exact role pair; this is record hygiene, not an authorization expansion; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Reject duplicate entries in combinationApproval.roles (len(roles) != len(set(roles)) -> E-COMBINATION-APPROVAL-DUPLICATE) and add uniqueItems to schema line 136; treat as a data-quality fix rather than a gate blocker.

findings.title: evidence_integrity dimension reports PASS while evidence errors exist
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged. evidence_check() (validator.py:260-300) appends Issue objects directly via issues.append(), bypassing fail() at 368-371 which is the only place dims[dimension] is set to FAIL. Registry-level checks at 400-410 do use fail(), but per-appointment failures (E-EVIDENCE-UNKNOWN, E-EVIDENCE-SUBJECT, E-EVIDENCE-ID-MISMATCH, E-EVIDENCE-REVOKED, etc.) do not. Probe with an unknown approval evidence_id: stage_b_role_ready=False with E-EVIDENCE-UNKNOWN, yet evidence_integrity=PASS. Note that stage_b at 561-565 also requires `not issues`, so readiness remains fail-closed.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no — the blocking error still forces stage_b_role_ready=False; only the per-dimension display is wrong.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — readiness and both authorization flags stay fail-closed; the impact is misdiagnosis/triage error, not an authorization decision; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Route all evidence_check() issue emission through fail() (or set dims[dimension]='FAIL' inside evidence_check) so the dimension matches the issue list; add a regression assertion on the dimension value, not only on readiness.

findings.title: Content hash is format-checked only and dangling evidence escapes hash checks
findings.affected_component: engine/validator.py (evidence_check hash regex; registry loop); schemas/team_assignment.schema.json (content_hash)
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged. validator.py:296-299 only checks re.fullmatch(r'[0-9a-fA-F]{64}', str(h)) for referenced evidence; there is no recomputation from source_ref. Registry loop 400-410 checks type/status/timestamp but never content_hash. Schema line 62 is type ['string','null'] with no pattern. Probes on valid_four_person.json: referenced hash='0'*64 -> ready=True, 0 issues; unreferenced record with content_hash='bad' -> ready=True, 0 issues.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: yes — both mutations returned ready=True; a referenced hash that does not correspond to its source cannot be distinguished from a valid one.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: authorization integrity conditional yes — if content_hash is intended as an authenticity anchor, forged evidence could satisfy a formal appointment; however the state contains no authoritative source bytes, so correspondence cannot be decided by this validator alone; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Define the hash contract first: either (a) document that content_hash is a lexical integrity token only and rename/reframe it, or (b) supply an authoritative source digest feed and compare it in evidence_check, applying the same check to every registry record including unreferenced ones. Add a schema pattern for the lexical rule. This requires investigation before a gate decision, so no silent downgrade.

findings.title: Duplicate evidence records under different IDs are not detected
findings.affected_component: engine/validator.py (evidence registry, evidence_check, acceptance decision_ref guard)
findings.v21_behaviour: Partially addressed only for CANDIDATE_ACCEPTANCE. V2.1 added decision_ref plus a cross-appointment reuse guard at validator.py:325-335 and ID/key consistency at 275-277, but there is still no registry-level content duplicate detection: a deep copy of an evidence record under a second ID with a matching evidence_id field passes. Probes: adding an exact copy of e-acc-C-P1-RESEARCH_OWNER under '-copy' -> ready=True; pointing CONTINUE_STOP_OWNER.approval.evidence_id at a copy of the RESEARCH_OWNER PRODUCT_OWNER_APPROVAL evidence -> ready=True; same for onboarding evidence -> ready=True. Non-acceptance evidence is bound only to candidate (subject='C-P1'), not to role, so copies are reusable across roles of one candidate.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: yes — independent probes produced stage_b_role_ready=True with one underlying approval/onboarding artifact reused for two roles.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: authorization integrity yes — distinct per-role evidence can be simulated by copying one record, weakening the role-approval boundary; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Add registry-level duplicate detection over the semantic tuple (evidence_type, source_ref, recording_authority, timestamp, subject, content_hash) and emit E-EVIDENCE-DUPLICATE; extend role binding (subject/evidence fields) to PRODUCT_OWNER_APPROVAL, FORMAL_APPOINTMENT and ONBOARDING, not only CANDIDATE_ACCEPTANCE.

findings.title: Evidence timestamp is not checked against its source or supported decision
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged in substance. validator.py:290-292 only calls valid_timestamp() (240-247: ISO parse plus timezone awareness); there is no comparison with the decision timestamp it supports or with source_ref. Probe: setting e-form-C-P1-RESEARCH_OWNER.timestamp to '1999-01-01T00:00:00+00:00' returned ready=True, 0 issues (EVID-06 DEFECT in V2.1 harness results).
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: yes — 1999 evidence satisfies a 2026 appointment and readiness stays True.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: authorization integrity conditional yes — backdated evidence can support a decision it could not have informed; cannot be adjudicated without an authoritative source timeline; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Specify a source-of-truth timestamp for each evidence type and check that evidence timestamp lies within the sourcing/decision interval (and is not earlier than the appointment it supports). Until that contract exists, document the limitation explicitly rather than claiming temporal integrity.

findings.title: No freshness or expiry model for acceptance, approval and appointment
findings.affected_component: engine/validator.py (role timestamp checks and ordering); policy/role_constraints.json (no freshness fields)
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged. validator.py:456-464 validates presence/timezone-awareness and ordering ts_a <= ts_p <= ts_f, but has no maximum age or expiry concept; combination approvals are only format-checked at 530-531. Probes: acceptance candidate_accepted_at='2020-01-01T00:00:00+00:00' -> ready=True; combination decision_timestamp='2019-01-01T00:00:00+00:00' -> ready=True (ST-02 and COMB-06 DEFECT in V2.1 harness).
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: yes — arbitrarily stale acceptance/approval timestamps still produce ready=True.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: authorization integrity conditional yes — an obsolete consent or approval can be presented as current; requires a governance-defined freshness window; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Define per-decision freshness/expiry in policy (e.g. max_age_days, valid_until, revalidation trigger) and enforce it in validator.py:456-464 and 530-531. This is a policy design decision, so keep OPEN pending investigation and do not infer a window from code.

findings.title: Combination decision timestamp is not ordered against candidate acceptance
findings.affected_component: engine/validator.py (role decision vs combination decision timestamps)
findings.v21_behaviour: Incidentally untouched by the N-15 fix. validator.py:463-464 does enforce ts_a <= ts_p <= ts_f for per-role timestamps, but the combination decision_timestamp at 530-531 is only passed through valid_timestamp(); it is never compared with the candidate's acceptance time. Probe: combination decision_timestamp='2026-11-26T00:00:00+00:00' with acceptance on 2026-11-27 returned ready=True, 0 issues (ST-03 DEFECT).
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: yes — an internally contradictory sequence (approval before acceptance) is reported Stage B ready.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: authorization integrity yes — the multi-role approval can predate the consent it depends on; this is derivable entirely from state data, no external authority needed; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Extend the ordering check to compare each combination approval decision_timestamp with max(candidate_accepted_at) for every held role, emitting E-COMBINATION-APPROVAL-TIMESTAMP-ORDER, and add ST-03 to the regression suite.

findings.title: Whitespace-only candidate reference accepted
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged for candidate references. validator.py:344-346 checks `ref != key or not ref`, and '   ' is truthy, so a registry entry keyed and referenced as three spaces is valid. The V2.1 meaningful_text() gate is used for evidence IDs at 266-269 but not for candidate_ref. The harness's ID-03 mutation is incidentally blocked by N-03 evidence-subject binding, but an independent probe that consistently rewrites candidate keys, role/appointment/combination refs, evidence IDs, subjects and appointment_refs to '   ' returned stage_b_role_ready=True, 0 issues.
findings.reproduction_status: reproduced (with a fully consistent mutation; the shipped harness mutation is blocked only incidentally by N-03 evidence binding)
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: yes — a role can be reported ready against a candidate identity consisting only of whitespace.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: authorization integrity yes — the identity gate is satisfiable without a real candidate identifier; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Apply meaningful_text() to candidate_ref in candidate_registry_check (validator.py:344-346) and to role/appointment/combination_approvals candidate_ref, emitting E-CANDIDATE-REF-INVALID, plus a schema minLength/pattern; add the fully consistent mutation as a regression case.

findings.title: No canonical identity linkage; one human can be represented as several identities to avoid combination approval
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged and explicitly declared OPEN_LIMITATION in the register. candidate_registry_check (validator.py:338-352) detects only exact duplicate candidate_ref strings; it has no alias, normalization or external-identity concept. V2.1 harness ID-07 produced E-ACCEPTANCE-APPOINTMENT/E-COMBINATION-APPROVAL-MISSING/E-EVIDENCE-SUBJECT and ready=False, i.e. incidental blocking from N-03 evidence binding and the missing exact-key approval — not from identity canonicalization. A carefully constructed split with per-alias evidence is not detectable by any code path in validator.py.
findings.reproduction_status: reproduced (code-level limitation; harness ID-07 is blocked incidentally, not by any identity check)
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: yes in principle — distinct aliases for one human can evade the multi-role combination approval and hard-incompatibility checks; not independently driven to ready=True in this follow-up because doing so requires a full synthetic alias dossier.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: authorization integrity yes — role-compatibility/combination-approval gates can be bypassed by alias splitting; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Introduce an authoritative person/identity identifier (or a documented alias set) in policy/state and require all role/appointment/evidence records to resolve to one canonical subject before compatibility checks; until such an authority is defined this cannot be fixed inside the validator alone — keep OPEN for investigation.

findings.title: No revocation or decision-history semantics
findings.v21_behaviour: Partially improved by the N-03 fix. V2.1 schema lines 70-71 declare evidence.revoked/revoked_at and validator.py:278-280 emits E-EVIDENCE-REVOKED when a referenced evidence record is revoked. Independent probes: evidence revoked=true and revoked_at set both now yield ready=False with E-EVIDENCE-REVOKED. However role-level/combination-level revocation and any history field remain schema-illegal (additionalProperties:false at schema lines 75, 122, 132) and produce E-SCHEMA rather than being evaluated; probes on roles.RESEARCH_OWNER.formal.revoked, combination_approvals[0].revoked and roles.RESEARCH_OWNER.history all returned E-SCHEMA. No decision-history/supersession semantics exist.
findings.reproduction_status: partially reproduced — evidence-level revocation is now handled; decision-history and role/combination revocation remain unsupported (fail-closed via E-SCHEMA)
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no for the residual part — unsupported fields are rejected, so no revoked decision currently produces ready=True; the residual gap is loss of expressiveness/auditability rather than a false readiness claim.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: authorization integrity partial — a formally revoked role decision cannot be represented or evaluated, so a superseded decision could remain recorded as active if it were expressed in a richer state format; current V2.1 state is fail-closed; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Define revocation and decision-history semantics (revoked_by, revoked_at, supersedes, effective interval) for role/approval/appointment/combination records, add them to the schema and evaluate them before readiness. Keep OPEN pending that design decision; do not treat the N-03 evidence-revocation addition as closure of N-14.

findings.title: No timestamp format/pattern in schema and no FormatChecker; timestamps not validated by JSON Schema
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged. Schema lines 64, 79, 89, 99, 107, 141 still declare timestamp fields as ['string','null'] with no format/pattern; $id remains relative (line 3). structural_schema_errors (validator.py:220-229) constructs cls(schema) without a format_checker. The engine's valid_timestamp (240-247) does enforce ISO parsing plus timezone awareness, but only on gated fields (409, 458, 530), not on recognition.decision_date or other untaxed fields. Probe: setting roles.RESEARCH_OWNER.recognition.decision_date='2026-01-01T00:00:00' (naive) returned ready=True, 0 issues. Environment check: jsonschema 4.26.0 FormatChecker has no date-time checker, so merely declaring format=date-time would not help here.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no — the naive value used in the probe is in an ungated field; all readiness-relevant timestamps are still required to be timezone-aware by validator.py:409/458/530.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — no false readiness and both authorization flags remain NO; the impact is schema-level diagnostic fidelity; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Document that the schema is structural-only and that lexical timestamp enforcement lives in engine code; if schema-level validation is desired, add a pattern for RFC3339-with-offset and pass an explicit FormatChecker (date-time checker is unavailable in this environment, so a pattern is the portable option).

findings.title: content_hash has no schema pattern; engine regex applies only to referenced evidence
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged and overlapping N-07. Schema line 62 types content_hash as ['string','null'] with no pattern. The 64-hex regex exists only in evidence_check (validator.py:296-299) for referenced records; registry loop 400-410 omits it. Probe: an unreferenced evidence record with content_hash='bad' returned ready=True, 0 issues. This is the schema-facet of the unresolved hash contract recorded under N-07.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: yes technically — an unreferenced record with a malformed hash does not block readiness; however unreferenced evidence cannot itself support an appointment, so the direct readiness impact is nil.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: authorization integrity conditional yes for the referenced-hash facet (see N-07); no additional impact for the dangling-record facet; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Resolve the hash contract under N-07 first; then add a schema pattern for the lexical rule and apply the same regex to every registry record, referenced or not.

findings.title: Unresolvable local $ref raises unhandled _WrappedReferencingError
findings.affected_component: engine/validator.py (structural_schema_errors, schema exception tuple, terminal schema handling)
findings.v21_behaviour: Incidentally fixed by the N-15 remediation and independently verified here. validator.py:24-40 builds _SCHEMA_EXCEPTION_TYPES including referencing PointerToNowhere/Unresolvable/NoSuchResource/InvalidAnchor and jsonschema RefResolutionError/_WrappedReferencingError; 220-233 catches those as E-SCHEMA-REFERENCE (and container/type errors as E-SCHEMA-INVALID); 378-389 makes schema failure terminal with all dimensions FAIL. Independent probe loading V2.1 tests/fixtures/unresolvable_ref_schema.json as the schema and validating valid_four_person.json returned stage_b_role_ready=False with a single E-SCHEMA-REFERENCE issue and no exception. Original severity retained; status reflects verification, not a downgrade.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no — the failure is now fail-closed with readiness NO; pre-fix it crashed without ever producing a positive readiness claim.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — no positive authorization can be inferred from a schema error before or after the fix; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: None required for closure; keep the MEDIUM row in the register with status verified_closed and add a permanent regression test for the unresolvable-$ref schema so a future exception-tuple regression is detected.

findings.title: Fallback subset silently ignores several JSON Schema keywords and can crash on boolean subschemas
findings.v21_behaviour: Source unchanged. validate_schema (validator.py:144-209) still supports only $ref, type, required, properties, additionalProperties, enum and items. Direct read-only probes: validate_schema({'properties':{'x':{'uniqueItems':True}}}, {'x':[1,1]}) returned [] (keyword silently ignored); validate_schema({}, False) raised TypeError (boolean subschema). However structural_schema_errors (220-238) uses full jsonschema whenever importable, and this environment has jsonschema 4.26.0, so the fallback is dormant; the re-audit also proved parity on the shipped schema. No production path exercised the fallback in any probe.
findings.reproduction_status: reproduced (latent — direct calls to the fallback reproduce both gaps; the CLI/validator path is dormant because jsonschema is installed)
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no in the current environment — full Draft 2020-12 validation is active for every CLI/validator call; readiness decisions never traverse the subset in these probes.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no currently; authorization integrity would be at risk only if the engine were deployed without jsonschema; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Either remove the fallback and fail closed with a clear E-SCHEMA-ENGINE issue when jsonschema is unavailable, or harden validate_schema (boolean schemas, uniqueItems, pattern, if/then) and add parity tests. Pin/document jsonschema as a deployment dependency in the interim.

findings.title: Evidence dict key vs evidence_id field consistency unchecked
findings.v21_behaviour: Partially fixed by N-03. validator.py:275-277 now emits E-EVIDENCE-ID-MISMATCH when a referenced record's evidence_id field differs from the registry key used to resolve it; probe with key e-acc-C-P1-RESEARCH_OWNER and field 'e-forged-id' returned ready=False with E-EVIDENCE-ID-MISMATCH. The registry loop (400-410) still does not compare key with field, so the register's original E06 case (key 'e1', field 'e999', unreferenced) still returns ready=True with no issue in an independent probe. The N-03 fix therefore did not fully cover S-05.
findings.reproduction_status: partially reproduced — original E06 unreferenced mismatch still accepted; referenced mismatches now blocked
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no for the residual part — an unreferenced inconsistent record cannot support any appointment; referenced inconsistencies are now blocked.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — no false readiness path remains for referenced evidence; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Add key/field consistency to the registry loop at 400-410 (emit E-EVIDENCE-ID-MISMATCH for every record), and add the original E06 case as a regression test.

findings.title: Schema $id is a relative URI
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged: $id is still the bare token 'm001-team-assignment-state-v2'. All $refs are local '#/$defs/...' strings resolved by validator.py:152-160 (subset) or by jsonschema against the in-memory schema, and no external reference is loaded in any code path. No behavioral difference observed.
findings.reproduction_status: reproduced (static property; local-only resolution confirmed by source review)
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no — no reference resolution depends on an absolute base URI in the shipped schema.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — no external fetch or identity/authorization effect; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Document that only local refs are supported, or adopt an absolute namespaced $id if the schema is ever published/shared. No gate impact.

findings.title: No uniqueItems/minItems on appointments or approvals; duplicate approvals overwrite by key
findings.v21_behaviour: Partially improved. Appointment duplicates are now explicitly rejected by validator.py:479-489 (E-CANDIDATE-DUPLICATE), which was already present in V2, and schema still lacks uniqueItems/minItems on appointments/combination_approvals. In the combination-approval loop, approval_map[(candidate, pair_key)] = ca at 503-511 is last-wins; appending an identical copy of the single combination approval to valid_four_person.json returned ready=True, 0 issues. Each record is still individually validated (outcome/rationale/evidence/timestamp), so a REJECTED duplicate would still emit E-COMBINATION-APPROVAL-REJECTED.
findings.reproduction_status: partially reproduced — combination-approval duplicates still schema-legal and overwrite by key; appointment duplicates are rejected by engine code
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: yes technically (ready=True with a duplicated approval) but not materially — the duplicate carries identical decisions and all records are individually validated, so no additional appointment is authorized.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — no false approval is produced by the duplicate itself; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Add uniqueItems to appointments and combination_approvals and reject exact/duplicate keys explicitly (E-COMBINATION-APPROVAL-DUPLICATE) instead of silent last-wins.

findings.title: Uncaught RecursionError on deeply nested JSON
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged. cli/validate.py:38-49 catches only (DuplicateKeyError, ValueError); engine/validator.py:110-133 calls json.loads at line 129 with no depth guard. Independent command `python -B C:\...\M001_TEAM_ASSIGNMENT_ENGINE_V2_1\cli\validate.py --state C:\...\V2_REAUDIT\tests\cases\c02_deep_5000_arrays.json` (cwd = V2.1 root) produced exit 1, empty stdout and a RecursionError traceback from json/__init__.py via load_json_strict. -B was used to avoid writing bytecode into protected directories.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no — the process fails closed with no readiness claim; the defect is output/exception handling only.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — no data is written and no authorization is inferred; availability of diagnostics is degraded; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Catch RecursionError in cli/validate.py:46 and return a structured E-INPUT-INVALID result with exit 2; optionally impose an explicit nesting-depth limit in load_json_strict. Add both deep-array and deep-object cases to the CLI regression suite.

findings.title: UnicodeEncodeError on lone surrogate escape echoed into human report
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged. cli/validate.py:57 prints the raw human report; human_report (validator.py:568-585) interpolates unescaped field values; json_result (588-592) uses json.dumps with default ensure_ascii=True and is safe. Independent command `python -B C:\...\V2_1\cli\validate.py --state C:\...\V2_REAUDIT\tests\cases\c04d_json_lone_surrogate_escape.json` on cp1252 stdout produced exit 1, empty stdout and UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\ud800' at cli/validate.py:57. No V2.1 sanitization was added.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no — fails closed before any readiness claim reaches stdout; the structured --json-only path is unaffected.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — no authorization effect; the raw value originates in caller-supplied input; confidentiality no (no new disclosure beyond the supplied file).
findings.recommended_resolution: Reject unpaired surrogate code points in load_json_strict, or emit the human report through an escaping/sanitizing writer (or default to json-only on encoding failure). Add the c04d case to CLI regressions.

findings.title: Relative --state anchored to V2; ../ escapes root (read-only)
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged apart from ROOT now pointing at V2.1. cli/validate.py:8-9, 33-36 resolve a relative --state as ROOT / state_path and report only state_path.name. Independent command from cwd=V2.1 root: `python -B .\cli\validate.py --state ..\M001_TEAM_ASSIGNMENT_ENGINE_V2_REAUDIT\tests\cases\c10_relative_state.json` produced a normal report (exit 1), Source: c10_relative_state.json, proving a file outside V2.1 was read. The path is used only by Path.read_bytes() (validator.py:110-116); --json-out was not used.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no — path anchoring does not change validation logic; the outside-root state still failed validation normally.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — read-only, deterministic, basename-only echo; no write or authorization effect; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Document that callers should pass absolute paths; optionally resolve from cwd or add an explicit allowed-root policy if the tool is ever exposed to untrusted callers.

findings.title: All OSError variants collapsed to E-FILE-NOT-FOUND
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged. validator.py:113-116 catches every OSError and raises ValueError('E-FILE-NOT-FOUND: %s' % exc.__class__.__name__); cli/validate.py:46-49 derives the code from the first token. Independent command passing the REAUDIT tests\cases directory as --state returned exit 2 with `ERROR E-FILE-NOT-FOUND ...: E-FILE-NOT-FOUND: PermissionError` (the re-audit saw IsADirectoryError) — same collapsed code/message shape as a missing file.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no — clean exit 2 with readiness NO for all these input errors.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — diagnostic message quality only; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Map OSError subclasses to distinct codes (E-FILE-NOT-FOUND, E-FILE-IS-DIRECTORY, E-FILE-PERMISSION, E-FILE-IO) while keeping the same fail-closed exit 2.

findings.title: Duplicate-key error omits JSON nesting path
findings.v21_behaviour: Unchanged. validator.py:121-126 raises DuplicateKeyError('E-DUPLICATE-JSON-KEY: %s' % k) with only the key name; no loc/path is threaded through json.loads. Independent command on V2_REAUDIT/tests/cases/c01_dup_nested_approval.json returned exit 2 with `E-DUPLICATE-JSON-KEY: basis` and no indication that the duplicate was under roles.RESEARCH_OWNER.approval.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no — duplicate keys are still rejected cleanly with exit 2 and readiness NO.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — triage/diagnostic quality only; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Track a path stack in the object_pairs_hook (or pre-scan with a streaming parser) and include it in the error message; keep the top-level code unchanged.

findings.title: Declared policy fields are never consumed by the validator; policy provenance partly self-referential
findings.v21_behaviour: Partially improved but reproduced. V2.1 consumes roles, appointment_states, formal_appointment_states, evidence_types, verification_statuses, stage_b_dimensions, require_topology_approved_for_stage_b and the three combination lists. A read-only source count of quoted field names in validator.py showed zero references for missing_appointment_states, evidence_fields, acceptance_evidence_binding, timestamp_fields and require_combination_approval_for_multi_role; review_requirement on discouraged combinations is likewise not read (the requirement logic is hardcoded). policy.source (line 3) still cites the defect register and V2.1 remediation, so provenance is partly self-referential. Behaviour remains deterministic and equivalent to the hardcoded logic.
findings.affects_stage_b_readiness: no — the unused fields are declarative; all corresponding behavior is enforced by equivalent hardcoded conditions, so no readiness outcome changes.
findings.affects_participant_confidentiality_or_a: no — no authorization path is altered; the risk is drift between documented policy and enforced policy; confidentiality no.
findings.recommended_resolution: Either consume the declared fields (notably require_combination_approval_for_multi_role and acceptance_evidence_binding) or remove/mark them as informational; replace the self-referential source with an authoritative governance-document citation.
